crowhurst-surrey.intro: Crowhurst, in the Surrey lanes near Lingfield, maps one tree: a yew with a door in it. Around 1820 the vicar had the door fitted and put a bench and table inside the hollow, and in 1825 a choir sang in there. A seven-pound cannonball turned up in the trunk. The tree is 10.03 metres round and still alive by a photograph of September 2024. It stands at St George's church, free to visit.
crowhurst-surrey.meta_description: The Crowhurst Yew in Surrey: 10.03 metres round, with a door in its hollow trunk, a cannonball in its past and a choir that once sang inside.
crowhurst-surrey.question_meta: Crowhurst's oldest tree is the yew at St George's church, 10.03 metres round; probably over 800 years old, an estimate from its girth.
crowhurst-surrey.question_answer: Crowhurst's oldest and only mapped tree is the Crowhurst Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) east-north-east of St George's church in Surrey. The Ancient Yew Group's size class puts yews this big at probably over 800 years old. That is an estimate from its girth of 10.03 metres, and nobody has dated the tree.
crowhurst-surrey.question_context: The paper trail is better than the dating. A parish record says the yew was ten yards round in the time of Charles I, and by 1850 it measured ten yards and nine inches at five feet up. The survey's tape read 10.03 metres in 1999 and again in 2013, so the trunk has added less than a metre in nearly four hundred years, if the early figures can be trusted. Around 1820 the vicar had a door fitted to the hollow and placed a bench and table inside, room for ten to fourteen people, and a newspaper reported a choir singing in it in 1825. A seven-pound cannonball, supposed to date from the Civil War, was found in or embedded in the trunk. The roof of the hollow had fallen in by 1850. In 1999 the survey noted two gaps in the bole, much dead wood and a chain swallowed by new growth. There is a second Crowhurst in East Sussex with its own old yew, so check which one you are heading for.

faq.q: How old is the Crowhurst Yew?
faq.a: It has never been dated. Its girth puts it in the Ancient Yew Group's class of probably over 800 years, and a parish record shows it was already ten yards round under Charles I.

faq.q: Is there really a door in the tree?
faq.a: Yes. A vicar had one fitted around 1820, and the 1999 survey found it still in place, four feet high.

faq.q: Which Crowhurst is this?
faq.a: The one in Surrey, near Lingfield. Crowhurst in East Sussex is a different village with a different yew.

tandridge.intro: Tandridge's mapped tree has been given up for dead twice. The yew at the west end of St Peter's church was reported dying in 1831 and again in 1850, and sources of the next century found it recovered. It is a split, hollow mass with younger yews around it, probably layered from the parent, under a canopy once put at 250 feet across. The churchyard is free, a short distance from Oxted in Surrey.
tandridge.meta_description: The Tandridge Yew in Surrey: a split, hollow giant at St Peter's church, twice reported dying in the 1800s and still standing in 2021.
tandridge.question_meta: Tandridge's oldest tree is the split yew at St Peter's church; its girth class says probably over 800 years, an estimate and not a date.
tandridge.question_answer: Tandridge's oldest and only mapped tree is the Tandridge Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) at the west end of St Peter's church in Surrey. By the Ancient Yew Group's size class it is probably over 800 years old, an estimate. Its 10.92 metres was taken at ground level on a split, multi-stem mass.
tandridge.question_context: That big number needs its small print. The survey took 10.92 metres in 1999 only five centimetres off the ground, around a fluted mass of several stems, so it cannot be compared with a yew measured at chest height. Older figures taken five feet up run from about 30 feet in 1850 to between 32 and 37 feet across the years 1880 to 1999. The main stem fractured long ago, and in 1890 two great lateral trunks were measured at 10 feet and 13 feet 4 inches. Fire or smoke has darkened the cavity. Reports in 1831 and 1850 had the tree dying; sources from 1936 and 1958 describe a strong recovery, and a 1936 account gave its canopy a circle of 250 feet. The younger yews close by were probably layered from the parent, and the survey lists a second notable yew here with no measurements. St Peter's has Norman fabric at its earliest. A dated photograph from September 2021 shows the old tree standing.

faq.q: How big is the Tandridge Yew?
faq.a: The survey recorded 10.92 metres at ground level around a split, multi-stem mass. Figures taken five feet up have run between about 30 and 37 feet since 1850.

faq.q: Was it really dying?
faq.a: It was reported dying in 1831 and in 1850. Sources from 1936 and 1958 say it recovered strongly.

faq.q: How old is it?
faq.a: Nobody has dated it. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, which is an estimate.

wilmington-east-sussex.intro: Wilmington, under the Long Man hill figure on the South Downs, maps a yew that is one tree and looks like two. Its hollow trunks lean apart from a single massive base on props and chains, north of the 12th-century church of St Mary and St Peter. In 1850 a villager of 85 said it had not changed in 75 years. It measures 9.15 metres round, and the churchyard is free to walk into.
wilmington-east-sussex.meta_description: The Wilmington Yew below the Long Man in East Sussex: two hollow trunks leaning apart from one base, on props and chains, 9.15 metres round.
wilmington-east-sussex.question_meta: Wilmington's oldest tree is the twin-trunked yew at St Mary and St Peter; probably over 800 years old, an estimate from its 9.15 m girth.
wilmington-east-sussex.question_answer: Wilmington's oldest and only mapped tree is the Wilmington Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) north of the church of St Mary and St Peter in East Sussex. It is two hollow trunks on one base, 9.15 metres round. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, which is an estimate.
wilmington-east-sussex.question_context: Whether this counts as one tree or two has an answer, and the answer is the base. A 1997 Sussex tree book described the two trunks as the healed halves of a single stem, and the common base is why the Ancient Yew Group's survey gives the pair one figure. Each trunk was about 16 feet round in 1999, both fluted and hollow, and they slant away from each other so far that props and chains now hold them up. An 1848 topographical dictionary gave six yards round at two feet up. Two years later the Sussex Archaeological Collections called it one of the greatest antiquities of the place and printed the word of a villager of 85, who had known it for 75 years without seeing any change. The survey re-measured it in 2015, its newest dated record. Girth is a looser guide than usual on a split stem, so the age class should be read loosely too. Above the church, on the hill, is the Long Man of Wilmington.

faq.q: Is the Wilmington Yew one tree or two?
faq.a: One. Its two trunks rise from a single massive base, and a 1997 Sussex tree book called them the healed halves of one stem.

faq.q: How do you find it?
faq.a: It stands north of the church of St Mary and St Peter, recognisable by two leaning hollow trunks with props and chains.

faq.q: What is the hill figure above the church?
faq.a: The Long Man of Wilmington. The church and the yew lie below it, and the churchyard is free to walk into.

corhampton.intro: Corhampton in the Meon Valley maps one tree, and the church beside it owns its portrait. An early 18th-century watercolour is the first record of this tall female yew, whose branches reach across the churchyard path and root where they touch the ground. Fifteen props once held it, and one remains. The church is late Saxon, founded in 1020 on an artificial mound and dedicated to nobody. Free to visit, on the A32 in Hampshire.
corhampton.meta_description: The Corhampton Yew in Hampshire: a tall female yew with rooting branches, painted in the early 1700s, beside a Saxon church founded in 1020.
corhampton.question_meta: Corhampton's oldest tree is the female yew at its Saxon church, about 7.3 metres round; probably over 800 years old by girth, undated.
corhampton.question_answer: Corhampton's oldest and only mapped tree is the Corhampton Yew, a female European Yew (Taxus baccata) in the churchyard of the Saxon church in Hampshire. It measured 7.32 metres near the ground in 1998. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, an estimate from girth, and its newest dated record is 2011.
corhampton.question_context: The first record of this yew is a painting, and it came long before any tape. An early 18th-century watercolour owned by the church is its earliest record, and travel writers praised it again in 1865 and 1897. It has a clean, visible bole, with a large leading branch and a second one dividing at about seven feet. Those branches have spread across the path and taken root where they meet the ground, and the fifteen props that used to carry them are down to one. Measurements stay close together: 7.32 metres near the ground in 1998, 7.11 metres at 1.1 metres in 1999, and 7.16 metres at 1.4 metres in 2011. That last figure is the newest dated evidence for the tree, so a visitor's photograph would be useful. The foliage was healthy and green when the survey saw it in 1999. The church itself was founded in 1020 on an artificial mound and has no dedication.

faq.q: How old is the Corhampton Yew?
faq.a: Nobody has dated it. At just over seven metres round it falls in the Ancient Yew Group's class of probably over 800 years, which is an estimate.

faq.q: How old is Corhampton church?
faq.a: It is late Saxon, founded in 1020, built on an artificial mound and without a dedication to any saint.

faq.q: Is the yew still alive?
faq.a: The newest dated evidence we have is a measurement from 2011. If you visit, we would like to hear how it is.

stedham.intro: Stedham, just west of Midhurst, maps a yew that has grown over its own repairs. Steel wire put in to hold the hollow, outward-leaning trunk is now sunk inside new wood, and branches pour out of the top of the bole. An account of 1815 already called it very remarkable, hollow and flourishing. It grows south-west of St James's church, whose tower is dated 1673, in a free churchyard in West Sussex.
stedham.meta_description: The Stedham Yew in West Sussex: a hollow, leaning trunk that has swallowed the steel wire meant to hold it, measured since 1815.
stedham.question_meta: Stedham's oldest tree is the hollow yew at St James's church, 8.97 metres round; probably over 800 years old, an estimate from girth.
stedham.question_answer: Stedham's oldest and only mapped tree is the Stedham Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) south-west of St James's church in West Sussex. It measured 8.97 metres at the ground in 1999. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, an estimate, and nobody has dated it.
stedham.question_context: Much the same number has been written about this tree for two centuries. An account of 1815 gave 28 feet round a yard up, and called the yew hollow with a flourishing head. It was 28 feet 6 inches in 1880 and 28 feet in 1952, then 30 feet 9 inches at two feet in 1983. The survey found 29 feet 6 inches at the ground in 1999, and 29 feet 5 inches in January 2012 with the tape running over an undulating base. The heights vary, so these are best read as a long plateau and not as a measure of growth. A 1997 record gives 11 metres of height. The hollow trunk leans outward, and the steel wire once used to hold it has been enveloped by new wood, as has the dead timber crossing the hollow. St James's has a tower of 1673 and one window that looks Norman. The newest dated evidence for the tree is from January 2012.

faq.q: How old is the Stedham Yew?
faq.a: It has never been dated. Its size puts it in the Ancient Yew Group's class of probably over 800 years.

faq.q: What is the wire in the trunk?
faq.a: Steel wire was put in to hold the hollow, leaning trunk together, and new wood has since grown around it.

faq.q: When was it last recorded?
faq.a: The newest dated evidence we have is from January 2012, so a recent photograph would be welcome.

dunsfold.intro: Dunsfold's yew has concrete in it. The hollow trunk beside the south porch of the 13th-century church of St Mary and All Saints shows signs of being filled in, and yet growth from six places suggests it is renewing itself. In 1911 the Victoria County History called it probably one of the most ancient trees in Surrey. Visitors reach the churchyard through a small tunnel of yew, and it costs nothing.
dunsfold.meta_description: The Dunsfold Yew in Surrey: a hollow trunk filled with concrete by the south porch of a 13th-century church, entered through a yew tunnel.
dunsfold.question_meta: Dunsfold's oldest tree is the concrete-filled yew at St Mary and All Saints, 7.52 m round; probably over 800 years old by girth, undated.
dunsfold.question_answer: Dunsfold's oldest and only mapped tree is the Dunsfold Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) close to the south porch of St Mary and All Saints in Surrey. It measured 7.52 metres near the ground in 1998. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, an estimate, and it has not been dated.
dunsfold.question_context: There are two age claims in this churchyard and they are about different things. The Victoria County History of 1911 thought the old yew probably one of the most ancient trees in the county, without saying how ancient. A plaque on a newer yew nearby says that a yew has stood close to the door for 700 years, which is a claim about the spot and not about either trunk. The survey's size class is the third voice, and it says probably over 800 years, from girth alone. The tape has been steady: 23 feet in 1903, 24 feet 6 inches at three feet in 1955, 24 feet 9 inches at the base in 1998, and 24 feet 8 inches near the ground in 2013, the newest dated evidence we have. The trunk has been infilled with concrete, which the survey worried was a weight on the tree. New growth from six points suggests the old yew is renewing itself. The church dates from the 13th century.

faq.q: Why is there concrete in the Dunsfold Yew?
faq.a: Its hollow trunk shows evidence of being infilled with concrete. Nothing we have read says when or by whom.

faq.q: Is it 700 years old?
faq.a: That figure comes from a plaque on a newer yew and says a yew has stood near the door for 700 years. The old tree itself has not been dated.

faq.q: How do you find it?
faq.a: Enter the churchyard through the small yew tunnel. The old yew stands close to the south porch.

charlwood.intro: Charlwood, in Surrey just west of Gatwick, maps one tree: a yew that an account of 1850 already called decayed. It is a hollow shell with burned inner walls and a gap four feet wide, sparse on the west side and healthy on the east when last recorded in 2013. It grows south-east of St Nicholas's church, built about 1080, in a churchyard inside a conservation area. Free to walk into.
charlwood.meta_description: The Charlwood Yew in Surrey: a fire-blackened hollow shell near Gatwick, called decayed in 1850 and still growing when measured in 2013.
charlwood.question_meta: Charlwood's oldest tree is the hollow yew at St Nicholas's church, 7.21 metres round; probably over 800 years old by girth, undated.
charlwood.question_answer: Charlwood's oldest and only mapped tree is the Charlwood Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) south-east of St Nicholas's church in Surrey. It measured 7.21 metres at 90 centimetres in 1999. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, an estimate, and a badly damaged shell makes that loose.
charlwood.question_context: What survives of this old yew is a shell standing beside a church of about 1080, with slivers of new wood inside it and much fire damage on the inner walls. The entrance is four feet wide and was once netted with wire. In 2013 the foliage was sparse on the west side and healthy on the east, so the tree is partly dead and partly vigorous. Its record is short and argumentative. An 1850 account called it a decayed yew-tree on the south side of the church. A guide of 1936, The King's England, gave 28 feet round, a figure the Ancient Yew Group's survey judged to be a mistake. The survey's own tape read 23 feet 8 inches in 1999 and 23 feet 5 inches at three and a half feet in May 2013, which is the newest dated evidence for the tree. The churchyard of St Nicholas's lies in a conservation area.

faq.q: How old is the Charlwood Yew?
faq.a: It has not been dated. At 7.21 metres it just falls within the Ancient Yew Group's class of probably over 800 years.

faq.q: What happened to its inside?
faq.a: The hollow shell shows much fire damage on its inner walls. We have found no record of the cause.

faq.q: When was it last recorded?
faq.a: In May 2013, when it was re-measured, with sparse foliage on the west and healthy growth on the east.

coldwaltham.intro: Coldwaltham, on the edge of the Arun valley in West Sussex, maps a yew that has collected large claims. A gazetteer gave it 3,000 years, which the Ancient Yew Group calls unsupported, and a notice beside it says it is among the twelve oldest. Measured, it is 10.49 metres round near the ground, completely hollow, with two straight fluted branches rising from the shell. It stands north-west of St Giles's church, free to visit.
coldwaltham.meta_description: The Coldwaltham Yew in West Sussex: 10.49 metres round, completely hollow, regarded as the county's senior yew, its 3,000-year claim unsupported.
coldwaltham.question_meta: Coldwaltham's oldest tree is the hollow yew at St Giles's church; a 3,000-year claim is unsupported, its girth class says over 800.
coldwaltham.question_answer: Coldwaltham's oldest and only mapped tree is the Coldwaltham Yew, a female European Yew (Taxus baccata) north-west of St Giles's church in West Sussex. A gazetteer's 3,000 years is called unsupported by the Ancient Yew Group, whose size class says probably over 800. It has not been dated.
coldwaltham.question_context: The tape gives better evidence than the claims do. It read 34 feet 5 inches, 10.49 metres, at fifteen centimetres off the ground in 1999, and the same 34 feet 5 inches on a return visit in 2012, with 30 feet 9 inches at three feet up. In 1955 it was 35 feet at the ground. A 1997 record gives a height of 14 metres and a diameter of 296 centimetres. A published book on the trees of Sussex regards it as the county's senior veteran yew. A notice at the churchyard places it among the twelve oldest, which the group considers possible but which appears on no list. It is a female, and completely hollow, with major cavities at the base and many nails hammered into the bole. Two straight fluted branches rise from what remains, and a central branch is closing around old growth. The crown was thinner in 2012 than in 1999, and 2012 is the newest dated evidence. The Norman church was rebuilt in the 19th century.

faq.q: Is the Coldwaltham Yew 3,000 years old?
faq.a: That figure comes from a gazetteer and the Ancient Yew Group calls it unsupported. The tree has not been dated, and its size class says probably over 800 years.

faq.q: Is it the oldest yew in Sussex?
faq.a: A book on the trees of Sussex regards it as the county's senior veteran yew. Nobody has proved it by dating.

faq.q: Is it healthy?
faq.a: It is completely hollow, and its crown was thinner in 2012 than in 1999. That 2012 visit is the newest dated evidence we have.

tangmere.intro: Tangmere's yew outlived its own replacement. In the 1760s it was declared dead and another was planted in its place, and the new tree failed while the old one came back. It is a stout female, south of St Andrew's church near Chichester, with a leaning section held by chains carrying the main branch. In 1885 the Church Builder called it the finest in all the country round. The churchyard is free.
tangmere.meta_description: The Tangmere Yew in West Sussex: declared dead in the 1760s and replaced, then outlived its replacement. A female yew, 8.08 metres round.
tangmere.question_meta: Tangmere's oldest tree is the yew at St Andrew's church, written off in the 1760s; probably over 800 years old by girth, undated.
tangmere.question_answer: Tangmere's oldest and only mapped tree is the Tangmere Yew, a female European Yew (Taxus baccata) south of St Andrew's church in West Sussex. It measured 8.08 metres at 30 centimetres in 1999. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, which is an estimate, and its newest dated record is 2011.
tangmere.question_context: It takes some nerve for a tree to be replaced and then recover, and that is what the record says happened here. In the 1760s the yew was reported dead and another was planted in its place. The replacement failed, and the old yew came back. By the next century it was admired in print. The Illustrated London News carried it in February 1846, and the Church Builder of 1885 called it the finest in all the country round. A figure of 20 feet at a yard up was published in 1848. A letter of 1988 gave 24 feet 8 inches at three feet, and a re-measurement in 2011 gave 24 feet 4 inches at the same height. Below three feet the trunk's own growth distorts the reading. A 1997 record makes it 12 metres tall. New wood is being laid down on the inner surface, and a chained, leaning section now carries the main branch. A Saxon church on the site was replaced about 1100.

faq.q: Was the Tangmere Yew really declared dead?
faq.a: Yes. In the 1760s it was reported dead and another yew was planted to replace it. The new tree failed and the old one recovered.

faq.q: How old is it?
faq.a: It has not been dated. Its girth places it in the Ancient Yew Group's class of probably over 800 years, an estimate.

faq.q: When was it last recorded?
faq.a: The newest dated evidence we have is a re-measurement in 2011.

itchen-abbas.intro: Itchen Abbas maps a yew that may appear in a Saxon charter of 939, a claim made in a 1994 book that we have not been able to confirm from the charter. What is certain is more recent. The Ancient Yew Group has returned to this gnarled tree repeatedly up to 2024. It stands on a mound east of St John the Baptist's church, beside the River Itchen near Winchester, and the churchyard is free.
itchen-abbas.meta_description: The Itchen Abbas Yew near Winchester: on a mound by the River Itchen, said to appear in a Saxon charter of 939, re-measured up to 2024.
itchen-abbas.question_meta: Itchen Abbas's oldest tree is the yew by St John the Baptist's church; said to be in a charter of 939, by girth probably over 800 years.
itchen-abbas.question_answer: Itchen Abbas's oldest and only mapped tree is the Itchen Abbas Yew, a European Yew (Taxus baccata) on a mound east of St John the Baptist's church in Hampshire. The Ancient Yew Group's size class says probably over 800 years, an estimate. A 1994 book says a Saxon charter of 939 records it, which we could not confirm.
itchen-abbas.question_context: The charter is the prize and also the problem. The Sacred Yew, published in 1994, says a Saxon charter of 939 records this tree. We have not seen that on a primary source, so it stays a claim, though if true it would make the yew more than a thousand years old. The firmer record starts in 1839, the first year in the Ancient Yew Group's history file. The survey measured 7.77 metres at 45 centimetres in April 1999, and the group has returned in 2010, 2011, from 2017 to 2019, and in 2023 and 2024. At the latest visit the tree was in fairly good condition. Its huge side limbs have been removed, the crown is lower than in old photographs, and the lower branches are hollow. Another yew, a male nine feet round at one foot, stands on the path to the porch and should not be confused with it. The church has late 11th-century origins, and the present building is Victorian.

faq.q: Is the Itchen Abbas Yew in a Saxon charter?
faq.a: A 1994 book says a charter of 939 records it. We have not been able to confirm that from the charter itself.

faq.q: Which yew is the old one?
faq.a: The gnarled tree on the mound east of the church, beside the river. A smaller male yew stands on the path to the porch.

faq.q: Is it still alive?
faq.a: Yes. The Ancient Yew Group photographed it in 2024 and found it in fairly good condition.
